component.name: Metroid Prime Port
component.summary: Metroid Prime running natively, with randomizer and Archipelago support

description.p: A native recompilation of Metroid Prime. The game is played as it was released, on the host's own Vulkan driver, with no emulator in the loop and no disc image bundled: the port asks for your own copy of the disc on first launch.
Features:

ul.li: Randomizer, with a full world and layer sweep covering every area
Archipelago multiworld, over ws:// and wss://
Controller button prompts rebuilt for the device in use
Memory card saves in the GCI format the series used

description.p: This package contains no game assets. It will not play without a disc image you supply, and none is distributed with it.

Metroid Dread Samus bodies imported from your own Metroid Dread dump, a third-person camera with an aiming cannon arm, Morph Ball control rows and controller presets, a reworked resolution scale and dynamic resolution, lock-on free aim, a walk speed setting, a Phazon Beam cheat, many more Prime Remastered models, effects and lighting through the HDR scene, Remastered rain, snow and underwater flakes, and savestates that keep enemies' AI, generated pickups and debris and the music that was playing.

Suit colour customisation with a random colours button, the Fusion Suit from the F1 menu, a touch layout editor that adds your own buttons, deletes stock ones and sets per-control opacity, a fix for the crash in the Meta Ridley fight, Aurora graphics fixes (EFB alpha, partial copy clears, texture coordinate generation and minification), Ridley, Thardus, Flaahgra and Metroid Prime restored mid-fight by savestates, a check of the whole disc image against its Redump release, and safer save, movie and disc reads.

Fewer missing or wrongly sized Remastered effects (sprites without a size, shutdown behaviour of trails and child particles, particle depth bias and motion spread), water fogs that follow the Gravity Suit in Tallon Overworld and Phendrana, progressive beam upgrades for Archipelago, a likely fix for a crash after the Frigate escape on Android, and Windows builds from a plain Visual Studio setup.

Remastered clustered lighting for lit effects (the Ice Beam's charge collision first), every Remastered point-light effect lit, more effect elements converted so the last effects that failed whole now load, the original ELC2 lightning look, separate vertical sensitivity for mouse, touch and gyro aim, empty lock-on holding the camera pitch under direct aim, Archipelago and offline randomizer pickup jingles for the placed item and scanned artifact hints, savestate fixes for Omega Pirate, moving platforms and spider tracks, and Fungal Hall Access's beam doors unlocking.

More Remastered effects drawn with their own shaders (Ice Beam charge and impact shards, missile and fire sprites, disintegration, visor goo splats that now actually draw, visor rain runoff, refraction warps), soft particles, the Plasma Beam's swooshes, resuming boss fights from savestates, charged and combo shots ricocheting off reflective enemies as in the original, real manual gyro calibration, unlocked beam doors kept after copying user data into a new release folder, lower storage use on Android, and a fix for mouse clicks wrongly accepting the resume prompt.

Remastered effects now run their particle maths as Metroid Prime Remastered does, generated Gravity, Phazon and Power spider ball looks, the full Flaahgra theme imported from a PAL, JP or Trilogy disc, a stack_beams setting, a first-person FOV limit of 120, gyro aiming improvements, lower memory use on Android, and fixes for savestates, PAL menus and doors saved open.

Per-visor HUD opacity, a Remastered-style crosshair, an option to keep beam doors unlocked once opened, a Rumble toggle, an Android setting to turn the on-screen controls off, Remastered movement on moving and rotating platforms, and fixes for rapid charge locking the weapons, bombs after a savestate load in morph ball, twin-stick aim speed, credits layout on wide screens, Archipelago item ids and the Remastered Power charge effect.

Smooth right-stick turning at high frame rates, map rotation with one finger on touch (with an option to swap one- and two-finger gestures), lock-on no longer keeping Remastered movement going, and Driver workarounds settings with a more detailed GPU self-test.

Gyro aim, mouse sensitivity on the Quake/Source scale, Remastered actor shadows and a world-wide baked-lighting volume, Wave Beam trails and electric arcs, Remastered movement, map pickup kinds and room marks, new randomizer options, smoother dynamic resolution, a faster Remastered import, adjustable touch control opacity on Android, a graphics backend choice on Windows, and screenshots that are no longer blank.

Mouse and touch in the menus and map, optional Trilogy-style pointer aim, Remastered room animations, waterfalls and shader fixes, movement that matches retail at any tick rate, and a shared memory card with Dolphin.

Remastered impact effects for the Power Beam, Plasma Beam and missiles, Android touch buttons that name what they do in morph ball and menus, and a fix for visor static that could get the game killed for low memory.
Steadier X-ray and thermal reticles while walking, a scan lock that no longer drops when a scan finishes, and better crash logging on Android.

A searchable settings window, a separate vertical stick aim speed, mouse fixes in morph ball, smoother scan icons and visor reticles at high frame rates, animated visor static, and a fix for the thermal visor running out of memory.

Save import and conversion between Wii Trilogy, USA, PAL and Dolphin saves, the real PAL save format, USA 1.01 and 1.02 discs supported, a 1.00 compatibility option, prompts that follow rebinds, and Remastered sun cascades.
Smoother high-FPS presentation, rebindable menu buttons, aim and scan-speed options, and Remastered prop lighting fixes.
Improves controller remapping and projected-blend lighting in Remastered imports.
First packaged release.
